incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired: PD-12345 - inference-gpu-serving - GPU memory pressure on cluster-gpu-1
PagerDuty: Incident triggered for service `inference-gpu-serving` (PD-12345). Trigger reason: repeated CUDA OOMs / GPU memory pressure > 90% on node gpu-node-7. Link: https://pagerduty.com/incidents/PD-12345
alex: acked :eyes: I'm taking first action.
priya: seeing the same in metrics. GPU mem util at ~98% on node gpu-node-7, a few pods showing OOMKilled.
priya: snippet from nvidia-smi (node gpu-node-7):
```
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| NVIDIA-SMI 520.56.06    Driver Version: 520.56.06    CUDA Version: 12.1   |
| Fan  Temp  Perf  Pwr:Usage/Cap|         Memory-Usage         | GPU-Util  
| 30%   72C    P2    230W / 300W |  24576MiB / 24576MiB        |  99%
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```
josh: any recent rollout? Could be a model change or batch config. Check recent deploys.
priya: checked deploys - no production rollout in last 2 hrs. A few heavy inference jobs started at ~10:02 UTC (batch export) that might be noisy.
mei: I'm looking at pod logs for inference-ff-3: shows repeated errors: `cudaErrorMemoryAllocation` then `terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::bad_alloc'`.
mei: logs:
```
[2026-03-14T10:03:12Z] ERROR inference: CUDA out of memory trying to allocate 512 MiB
[2026-03-14T10:03:13Z] ERROR runtime: failed to run forward pass: cudaErrorMemoryAllocation
[2026-03-14T10:03:13Z] INFO kube: pod inference-ff-3 OOMKilled
```
alex: temporary mitigations: 1) drain gpu-node-7 of non-critical jobs 2) restart the worst offenders (one by one) 3) reduce runtime batch_size for heavy model routes. I'm going to cordon the node and evict batch jobs.
alex: running:
```
kubectl cordon gpu-node-7
kubectl get pods -n redwood-inference -o wide | grep gpu-node-7
kubectl delete pod inference-batch-22 -n redwood-inference
```
priya: FYI: scale-up won't be instant, but we can scale the gpu-pool from 4->6 nodes. Starting a horizontal scale request now.
priya: submitted autoscaler request: `scale pool gpu-prod-pool --nodes 6` (cloud request sent). ETA ~4-5m.
sre-rotation: escalated to SRE due to repeated OOMs. Taking over on-call coordination. I'll coordinate safe restarts and traffic mitigation.
sre-rotation: immediate mitigation plan: 1) throttle large-batch routes via runtime config 2) move critical traffic to smaller-ram model variant (fallback) 3) restart pods with larger reserved memory when possible.
sre-rotation: runtime API call to set per-route batch size to 1 (example):
```
POST /v1/config/routes/batch-size
{ "route": "/v1/generate", "batch_size": 1 }
```
mei: applied a temporary route config to reduce batch windows for `model=gpt-xl-8bit`. Monitoring.
mei: also started a rolling restart of the three worst pods (one at a time) to free up GPU memory.
alex: restarted inference-ff-3 successfully. Pod came back without OOM after restart.
priya: autoscaler reported two new GPU nodes provisioning, expected join in ~3m.
josh: customer-impact check: Support telemetry shows spike in 502s for hosted customers between 10:02-10:10 UTC. Top affected: acme-inc (5% of requests failed), partner-beta (3% failed). No major outage but degraded for a subset. I'm drafting a status page update.
josh: status page draft:
```
We are investigating elevated error rates for GPU inference. Some requests may see increased latency or failures. Engineers are mitigating. Affected customers: acme-inc, partner-beta.
```
priya: after the restart + throttle, error rate dropped. Metrics: 502 error rate from 7.1% -> 1.3% over 6 minutes. Latency 95p decreased from 2.4s -> 1.1s for critical routes.
sre-rotation: confirm: node gpu-node-7 still reporting high mem for queued batch jobs; new nodes came up and autoscaler placed two more pods, spread is improving.
sre-rotation: next steps: 1) keep throttle in place for 30m 2) keep node cordoned for now 3) schedule deeper investigation into memory growth (heap/kvcache leak) 4) open an incident ticket and assign to eng-runtime.
alex: created GH issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/issues/456 - title: "PD-12345: GPU memory pressure - investigate OOM patterns". Assigned to @mei and @josh.
mei: adding heap/KV cache checks to reproducer. Will run targeted profiling on the model serving path.
josh: notified support and posted status update: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/PD-12345 updated.
priya: will monitor for 20m then start lowering throttle if stable.
incident-bot: PD-12345 escalated to SRE and acknowledged by sro-rotation at 1765432155.
alex: quick note — if anyone needs to contact the customer teams, use the secure channel #support-incidents.
sre-rotation: leaving a short handoff note: I'm on-call until 11:30 UTC — if this regresses, page SRE again (PD escalation policy). I'm tagging the runtime oncall as follow-up: @alex, @mei, @josh.
priya: handoff acked. I'll stay watch and will escalate if errors climb above 3%.
josh: adding post-incident actions: add synthetic tests to catch large-batch memory pressure, add alert for sustained GPU mem > 90% for >3m, and add automatic route slowdown.
sre-rotation: creating incident incident-tracker ticket: INC-2026-789 and attaching logs.
incident-bot: PD-12345 auto-resolve check in 15m unless more alerts fire.
priya: thanks all — will update if anything changes.
alex: closing active mitigation. Leaving follow-up tasks in GH issue.
me: (typo) — mei: signing off brief watch.
